claim: Cyborg control of insect movement is promising for developing miniature, high-mobility, and efficient biohybrid robots.
source: Cyborg control of insect movement is promising for developing miniature, high-mobility, and efficient biohybrid robots.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of cyborg control technology, presented as an established viewpoint in the field.

claim: A nearly linear relationship between the stimulus burst duration and generated torque was observed.
source: A nearly linear relationship between the stimulus burst duration and generated torque was observed.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental measurements reported in the study.

claim: The stimulus-torque characteristic holds for burst durations of up to 500ms.
source: This stimulus-torque characteristic holds for burst durations of up to 500ms, corresponding to the stance and swing phase durations of medium to fast walking stick insects.
evidence: This is directly stated based on experimental observations and comparison to walking phase durations.

claim: Burst durations of up to 500ms correspond to the stance and swing phase durations of medium to fast walking stick insects.
source: This stimulus-torque characteristic holds for burst durations of up to 500ms, corresponding to the stance and swing phase durations of medium to fast walking stick insects.
evidence: This relates experimental parameters to known locomotion characteristics of stick insects.

claim: Hierarchical Bayesian modeling revealed that linearity of the stimulus-torque characteristic was invariant, with individually varying slopes.
source: Hierarchical Bayesian modeling revealed that linearity of the stimulus-torque characteristic was invariant, with individually varying slopes.
evidence: This is a key finding from the Bayesian statistical analysis performed in the study.

claim: Individual prediction of joint torques provides significant benefits for precise cyborg control.
source: Individual prediction of joint torques provides significant benefits for precise cyborg control.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results regarding applications to cyborg control.

claim: Hybrid insect–computer robots represent cutting-edge approaches to develop robots with locomotor performances comparable to those of insects.
source: Hybrid insect–computer robots (Krause et al., 2011; Li and Sato, 2018) represent cutting-edge approaches to develop robots with locomotor performances comparable to those of insects.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work in the field.

claim: Biohybrid cyborg robots have been engineered to manipulate their gait and flight through electrical stimulation of target muscles in various insects, including beetles, moths, and cockroaches.
source: such biohybrid, that is cyborg robots have been engineered to manipulate their gait and flight through electrical stimulation of target muscles in various insects, includings beetles (Sato, 2009; Sato and Maharbiz, 2010; Sato et al., 2015; Cao et al., 2016; Vo Doan et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2020; Kosaka et al., 2021), moths (Sane et al., 2007; Bozkurt et al., 2009; Hinterwirth et al., 2012; Ando and Kanzaki, 2017), and cockroaches (Sanchez et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Biohybrid cyborg robots do not require individual 'design', 'fabrication', and 'assembly' processes for each component because they use the body tissues of living insects.
source: The advantage of biohybrid (cyborg) robots is that they do not require individual 'design', 'fabrication', and 'assembly' processes for each component because they use the body tissues of living insects (Cao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of cyborg robots with citation support.

claim: Cyborg robots have low power consumption of a few milliwatts.
source: Moreover, cyborg robots have low power consumption, that is, a few milliwatts (Sato and Maharbiz, 2010).
evidence: This is a specific quantitative claim supported by citation.

claim: The greatest challenge in cyborg control comes with the inter-individual variability of animals.
source: Perhaps, the greatest challenge in cyborg control comes with the inter-individual variability of animals.
evidence: This is presented as an expert assessment of the field's challenges.

claim: A model formulated using the average data for a group cannot explain the characteristics of any individual in the group.
source: Past neurophysiological studies related to animal neural activity have discussed the failure of averaging-based approaches, in which a model formulated using the average data for a group cannot explain the characteristics of any individual in the group (Golowasch et al., 2002; Schulz et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior neurophysiological studies.

claim: Variable and non-periodic patterns in feeding behavior of Aplysia have been reported to be subject to strong inter-individual variation.
source: For example, variable and non-periodic patterns in feeding behavior of Aplysia have been reported to be subject to strong inter-individual variation (Horn et al., 2004; Brezina et al., 2005; Zhurov et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies on Aplysia.

claim: The prediction error of muscle models which are based on sample averages is very high and may be halved using individual-specific model.
source: In insect motor physiology, the prediction error of muscle models which are based on sample averages is very high (Blümel et al., 2012a) and may be halved using individual-specific model (Blümel et al., 2012b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to specific studies on insect muscle models.

claim: The retractor coxae is the primary muscle for propulsion in stick insects.
source: We focused on these three proximal muscles because the retractor coxae is the primary muscle for propulsion (Rosenbaum et al., 2010)
evidence: This is stated with citation support regarding muscle function.

claim: The pro/retractor coxae contributes to weight-dependent postural adjustment by regulating joint stiffness.
source: the pro/retractor coxae contributes to weight-dependent postural adjustment by regulating joint stiffness (Dallmann et al., 2019; Günzel et al., 2022)
evidence: This functional role is supported by citations.

claim: The levator trochanteris is important for postural termination and swing initiation.
source: the levator trochanteris is important for postural termination and swing initiation (Dallmann et al., 2017)
evidence: This functional role is supported by citation.

claim: When stick insects walk, they use the protractor to swing the leg forward during the swing phase.
source: When stick insects walk, they use the protractor to swing the leg forward during the swing phase
evidence: This describes the functional role of the protractor muscle during walking.

claim: When stick insects walk, they use the retractor to move the leg backward during the stance phase.
source: the retractor to move the leg backward during the stance phase
evidence: This describes the functional role of the retractor muscle during walking.

claim: When stick insects walk, they use the levator to initiate the stance-to-swing transition.
source: and levator to initiate the stance-to-swing transition (Rosenbaum et al., 2010; Dallmann et al., 2019; Günzel et al., 2022; Bässler and Wegner, 1983)
evidence: This describes the functional role of the levator muscle with citation support.

claim: Co-contraction of the protractor and retractor are known to vary based on the overall load distribution.
source: Moreover, co-contraction of the protractor and retractor are known to vary based on the overall load distribution, thus being important for postural control by regulating joint stiffness (Dallmann et al., 2019; Günzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as known behavior with citation support.

claim: Electrical stimulation of the protractor and retractor muscles generated forward and backward movements at the thorax–coxa (ThC) joint.
source: Accordingly, electrical stimulation of the protractor and retractor muscles generated forward and backward movements at the thorax–coxa (ThC) joint, as measured by a calibrated custom-made force transducer with a strain gauge held against the femur with known distance from the joint.
evidence: This describes the experimental observation of muscle stimulation effects.

claim: Stimulation of the levator muscle generated an upward movement at the coxa–trochanter (CTr) joint.
source: Stimulation of the levator muscle generated an upward movement at the coxa–trochanter (CTr) joint (Dallmann et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the experimental observation with citation support.

claim: The input–output relation (burst duration and generated torque) corresponded to a linear function or a power function with an exponent of less than 1.0.
source: The results indicate the input–output relation (burst duration and generated torque) corresponded to a linear function or a power function with an exponent of less than 1.0.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings.

claim: The relationship between burst duration and torque holds for burst durations up to 500ms for all animals.
source: Furthermore, the relationship holds for burst durations up to 500ms for all animals, corresponding to the duration of swing and stance phases in medium to fast walking stick insects (Dürr et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated based on experimental data with citation for comparison.

claim: Maximum torques for ThC and CTr joints were 60 µNm, 120 µNm, and 40 µNm.
source: Maximum torques for ThC and CTr joints were 60 µNm, 120 µNm, and 40 µNm (Dallmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This provides specific quantitative measurements with citation.

claim: The probabilistic nature of Bayesian models makes them appropriate for modeling 'uncertainty', as introduced by inter-individual variation.
source: The probabilistic nature of Bayesian models makes them appropriate for modeling 'uncertainty', as introduced by inter-individual variation (Gelman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a methodological justification supported by citation.

claim: Hierarchical model variants allow the inclusion of a hyperparameter, thus allowing for a parameter of choice to be drawn from yet another probabilistic distribution.
source: Furthermore, hierarchical model variants allow the inclusion of a hyperparameter, thus allowing for a parameter of choice to be drawn from yet another probabilistic distribution.
evidence: This describes a property of hierarchical Bayesian models.

claim: Hierarchical-model variants were used to account for inter-individual differences.
source: In our case, hierarchical-model variants were used to account for inter-individual differences (Watanabe, 2018).
evidence: This describes the methodological approach with citation.

claim: The hierarchical models can appropriately account for inter-individual variation of muscle properties for new unknown animals.
source: This suggests that, compared with other models, the hierarchical models can appropriately account for inter-individual variation of muscle properties for new unknown animals.
evidence: This is inferred from the model performance results.

claim: Linearity was an invariant feature of the stimulus-torque characteristic, whereas the slope of this characteristic varies among individual stick insects and with the applied voltage.
source: We conclude that linearity was an invariant feature of the stimulus-torque characteristic, whereas the slope of this characteristic varies among individual stick insects and with the applied voltage.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: The generated torque depends considerably less on the PWM voltage and frequency than on the burst duration.
source: These results are in line with those of existing studies on the properties of myogenic forces in other insect species (Cao et al., 2014; Blümel et al., 2012a; Harischandra et al., 2019): The generated torque depends considerably less on the PWM voltage and frequency (Blümel et al., 2012a; Harischandra et al., 2019) than on the burst duration, suggesting that the total number of subsequent input pulses is important.
evidence: This is stated with citation support from prior studies.

claim: The total number of subsequent input pulses is important for torque generation.
source: The generated torque depends considerably less on the PWM voltage and frequency (Blümel et al., 2012a; Harischandra et al., 2019) than on the burst duration, suggesting that the total number of subsequent input pulses is important.
evidence: This is inferred from the dependence on burst duration.

claim: Slow insect muscle essentially 'counts' incoming spikes within a given time window.
source: This is indeed expected for a slow insect muscle (Blümel et al., 2012a) that essentially 'counts' incoming spikes within a given time window.
evidence: This is stated as an expected property with citation support.

claim: Monitoring of torques in an intact animal resulted in a linear characteristic (for intervals up to 500ms) that would not be expected from isometric force measurements of isolated muscles.
source: Compared to the nonlinear properties of muscle, we demonstrated that our monitoring of torques in an intact animal resulted in a linear characteristic (for intervals up to 500ms) that would not be expected from isometric force measurements of isolated muscles.
evidence: This contrasts the current findings with expectations from isolated muscle studies.

claim: Changing the PWM frequency was found to be comparable to changing the number of spikes over a given period.
source: Furthermore, changing the PWM frequency was found to be comparable to changing the number of spikes over a given period, whereas changing the duty ratio was found to be comparable to varying the average voltage over a given period (see Appendix 1—figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated based on analysis shown in appendix figures.

claim: Changing the duty ratio was found to be comparable to varying the average voltage over a given period.
source: Furthermore, changing the PWM frequency was found to be comparable to changing the number of spikes over a given period, whereas changing the duty ratio was found to be comparable to varying the average voltage over a given period (see Appendix 1—figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated based on analysis shown in appendix figures.

claim: The comparison of the linear model (model 1–2) with the nonlinear model (model 2–2) using the WAIC for all conditions resulted in lower values for the linear model.
source: The comparison of the linear model (model 1–2) with the nonlinear model (model 2–2) using the WAIC for all conditions (muscle type and applied voltage) resulted in lower values for the linear model.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the model comparison results.

claim: Models with lower WAIC can generate predictive distributions closer to the true distribution while using fewer parameters.
source: Models with lower WAIC can generate predictive distributions closer to the true distribution while using fewer parameters (Watanabe, 2018)
evidence: This explains the interpretation of WAIC with citation.

claim: The experimental results obtained in this study can be adequately explained using a linear hierarchical Bayesian model (1-2).
source: suggesting that the experimental results obtained in this study can be adequately explained using a linear hierarchical Bayesian model (1-2).
evidence: This is concluded from the WAIC comparison results.

claim: The properties were linear for stimulus burst durations up to 500ms, which corresponds to the stance and swing phase durations of medium-speed to fast walking stick insects of the species Carausius morosus.
source: Moreover, the properties were linear for stimulus burst durations up to 500ms. This linearity region corresponds to the stance and swing phase durations of medium-speed to fastwalking stick insects of the species Carausius morosus (Dürr et al., 2018).
evidence: This relates the experimental findings to natural locomotion with citation.

claim: The magnitudes of the joint torques generated by the protractor, retractor, and levator were comparable to those for resisted movement during stick-insect walking.
source: The magnitudes of the joint torques generated by the protractor, retractor, and levator were comparable to those for resisted movement during stick-insect walking, for example coxa-trochanter joint depression during stance (Dallmann et al., 2016).
evidence: This compares experimental torques to natural walking with citation.

claim: The estimated stimulus-torque characteristic captures the natural dynamic properties of leg muscles during walking in terms of both the duration of excitation and maximum torque.
source: This suggests that the estimated stimulus-torque characteristic captures the natural dynamic properties of leg muscles during walking in terms of both the duration of excitation and maximum torque.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison with natural walking parameters.

claim: The hierarchical nonlinear model (model 2–2) would be more appropriate for estimating properties related to longer time scales, such as those associated with the complete range of muscle excitation.
source: However, the hierarchical nonlinear model (model 2–2) would be more appropriate for estimating properties related to longer time scales, such as those associated with the complete range of muscle excitation.
evidence: This is a speculation about model applicability beyond the tested range.

claim: Motion Hacking is defined as a technique for controlling insect leg movements through external electrical stimulation, while retaining the insect's own nervous system and sensorimotor loops.
source: In previous studies, we defined Motion Hacking (Owaki et al., 2019; Owaki and Dürr, 2022) as a technique for controlling insect leg movements through external electrical stimulation, while retaining the insect's own nervous system and sensorimotor loops.
evidence: This defines the Motion Hacking approach with citations.

claim: The Motion Hacking approach requires a collaborative effort of engineering and biology in order to elucidate how adaptive walking ability of insects may be exploited for biohybrid control of motor flexibility.
source: This approach requires a collaborative effort of engineering and biology in order to elucidate how adaptive walking ability of insects may be exploited for biohybrid control of motor flexibility.
evidence: This describes the interdisciplinary nature of the approach.

claim: The Motion Hacking method strives to observe the adaptation process in the insect's own sensorimotor system as leg movements are intentionally controlled by a human operator.
source: The Motion Hacking (Owaki et al., 2019; Owaki and Dürr, 2022) method strives to observe the adaptation process in the insect's own sensorimotor system as leg movements are intentionally controlled by a human operator, so as to reveal hidden mechanisms underlying natural locomotion.
evidence: This describes the goal of the Motion Hacking method with citations.

claim: Research on insect cyborg control has addressed aspects of flight control, gait control, and controlling jellyfish propulsion.
source: Thus far, research on insect cyborg control has addressed aspects of flight control (Sato, 2009; Sato and Maharbiz, 2010; Sato et al., 2015; Kosaka et al., 2021; Sane et al., 2007; Bozkurt et al., 2009; Hinterwirth et al., 2012), gait control (Cao et al., 2016; Vo Doan et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2020; Ando and Kanzaki, 2017; Sanchez et al., 2015), and controlling jellyfish propulsion (Xu and Dabiri, 2020a; Xu et al., 2020b; Xu et al., 2020c).
evidence: This summarizes prior research areas with extensive citations.

claim: The main objective of previous cyborg studies was to convert target animals into cyborgs, with little examination of the control mechanisms and/or muscle properties involved.
source: In contrast to our present study, the main objective of the mentioned studies was to convert target animals into cyborgs, with little examination of the control mechanisms and/or muscle properties involved.
evidence: This contrasts the current study with prior work.

claim: PWM pulse bursts were used to mimic motor neuron commands during insect locomotion.
source: Here, we used PWM pulse bursts to mimic motor neuron commands during insect locomotion, and selected key muscles to estimate stimulus-torque characteristics reliably and in very short time.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: Bayesian statistical modeling was used to tell which parameters were subject to inter-individual variation and which were not.
source: Then, we used Bayesian statistical modeling to tell which parameters were subject to inter-individual variation and which were not.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach.

claim: A systematic engineering intervention to an otherwise intact animal motor system can yield a simple, technically exploitable description of motor system properties.
source: Our finding of linear characteristics with inter-individual variation of slope show compellingly how a systematic engineering intervention to an otherwise intact animal motor system can yield a simple, technically exploitable description of motor system properties.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the methodological approach.

claim: This description could not have been obtained by methods addressing isolated neural circuits or partial anatomical structures, but required the physical intactness of the natural system.
source: We argue that this description could not have been obtained by methods addressing isolated neural circuits or partial anatomical structures, but required the physical intactness of the natural system.
evidence: This argues for the necessity of the intact-animal approach.

claim: Compared to the nonlinear activation and contraction dynamics of insect muscles, the joint torque generated through electrical stimulation increases linearly with the duration of the stimulus, particularly during the stance and swing phases that characterize stick insect locomotion.
source: The contributions of this research are as follows: (1) this study demonstrates that compared to the nonlinear activation and contraction dynamics of insect muscles, the joint torque generated through electrical stimulation increases linearly with the duration of the stimulus, particularly during the stance and swing phases that characterize stick insect locomotion
evidence: This is stated as a key contribution of the research.

claim: The study introduces a hierarchical Bayesian model that allows for a reliable and simple description of the individual differences observed in neuromuscular system parameters.
source: (2) it introduces a hierarchical Bayesian model that allows for a reliable and simple description of the individual differences observed in neuromuscular system parameters.
evidence: This is stated as a key contribution of the research.

claim: Animal locomotion is not solely governed by the brain and nervous system but also relies on the physical properties of the body and its interactions with the environment.
source: Animal locomotion is not solely governed by the brain and nervous system but also relies on the physical properties of the body and its interactions with the environment (Chiel et al., 2009; Nishikawa et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Arthropods effectively utilize mechanical properties and environmental interactions in their locomotion.
source: Arthropods, in particular, effectively utilize mechanical properties and environmental interactions in their locomotion.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about arthropods.

claim: Spiders exhibit joint stiffness nonlinearity and hysteresis.
source: Studies have revealed various related strategies, including the joint stiffness nonlinearity and hysteresis in spiders (Blickhan, 1986)
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Insects generate large motor outputs during escape maneuvers and posture stabilization by adjusting the joint stiffness.
source: generation of large motor outputs during escape maneuvers (Card, 2012) and posture stabilization (Blickhan, 1986) by adjusting the joint stiffness
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Web-making spiders use mechanical sensing based on frequency characteristics that vary with the joint stiffness and posture.
source: mechanical sensing based on frequency characteristics that vary with the joint stiffness and posture in web-making spiders (Blickhan and Barth, 1985; Mhatre et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Cockroaches exhibit transitions in movement patterns in response to mechanical interactions with the environment.
source: transitions in movement patterns in response to mechanical interactions with the environment (Othayoth et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Cockroaches exhibit transitions in the coordinated movements of the body and legs.
source: and transitions in the coordinated movements of the body and legs (Wang et al., 2022) in cockroaches.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Sponberg et al. conducted experiments by perturbing neural feedback through artificial interventions on muscle action potentials (MAPs) in cockroaches Blaberus discoidalis.
source: Similarly, to elucidate the animal locomotion mechanisms emerging from such complex interactions, Sponberg et al., 2011a; Sponberg et al., 2011b conducted experiments similar to those in our study by perturbing neural feedback through artificial interventions on muscle action potentials (MAPs) in cockroaches Blaberus discoidalis (L.).
evidence: This describes prior related work with citations.

claim: Stick insects were fixed and not walking in the experimental setup.
source: First, as in many neurophysiological experiments (Berg et al., 2012; Lepreux et al., 2019), stick insects were fixed and not walking in the experimental setup (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes a limitation of the experimental setup with citations.

claim: Stick insects spend a lot of their lifetime at rest, for example in camouflage.
source: Although there are only few studies on the natural dispersal behavior of stick insects, it is clear that they spend a lot of their lifetime at rest, for example in camouflage.
evidence: This is stated as general knowledge about stick insect behavior.

claim: The tendency of stick insects to attain camouflage postures can be exploited in experiments, as it is relatively easy to restrain active, spontaneous leg movements in an experimental setup.
source: Their tendency to attain camouflage postures can be exploited in experiments, as it is relatively easy to restrain active, spontaneous leg movements in an experimental setup.
evidence: This explains how stick insect behavior facilitates experiments.

claim: The possibility to conduct combined motion capture and EMG recordings in freely walking stick insects suggests that Motion Hacking during unrestrained, voluntary locomotion will be feasible in the future.
source: Nevertheless, the possibility to conduct combined motion capture and EMG recordings in freely walking stick insects (Dallmann et al., 2019; Günzel et al., 2022; Dallmann et al., 2017; Bidaye et al., 2018) suggests that Motion Hacking during unrestrained, voluntary locomotion will be feasible in the future.
evidence: This is a speculation about future possibilities based on cited prior work.

claim: There is considerable discrepancy between the PWM signals generated by the Raspberry Pi microcontroller and the natural firing patterns of motor neuron pools.
source: Whereas the range of PWM burst duration and the joint torques generated are well within the physiological range, there is still considerable discrepancy between the PWM signals generated by our Raspberry Pi microcontroller and the natural firing patterns of motor neuron pools (Günzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the experimental approach with citation.

claim: The simplified PWM signal used could be applied more than 50 times in a sequence without causing muscle fatigue.
source: So far, it is re-assuring that the simplified PWM signal used here could be applied more than 50 times in a sequence without causing muscle fatigue, that is with a sustained level of generated torque.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental observations.

claim: The maximum voltage of 4 V used did not cause abnormal motion that could be attributed to cross-talk stimulation of sensory afferents.
source: The maximum voltage of 4 V used here did not cause abnormal motion that could be attributed to cross-talk stimulation of sensory afferents.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental observations.

claim: Unintended electrical stimulation of sensory afferents was negligible.
source: Therefore, we conclude that unintended electrical stimulation of sensory afferents was negligible.
evidence: This is concluded from the absence of abnormal motion.

claim: Control measurements confirmed that muscles other than those stimulated by the electrodes were not active and did not generate force.
source: Moreover, control measurements confirmed that muscles other than those stimulated by the electrodes were not active and did not generate force, as it would be expected from unintended stimulation via cross-talk.
evidence: This is stated based on control measurements.

claim: The activation of sensory organs during cyborg control is an interesting topic, with strong potential for expanding the concept of Motion Hacking.
source: More generally, the activation of sensory organs during cyborg control is an interesting topic, with strong potential for expanding the concept of Motion Hacking.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Twenty adult female Carausius morosus from the laboratory colony at Bielefeld University were tested in 2018.
source: We tested 20 adult female Carausius morosus from our laboratory colony at Bielefeld University in 2018.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects.

claim: The animals were raised under a 12 hr:12 hr light:dark cycle at a temperature of 23.9 ±1.3 °C.
source: The animals were raised under a 12 hr:12 hr light:dark cycle at a temperature of 23.9 ±1.3 °C (mean ± S.D).
evidence: This describes the animal husbandry conditions.

claim: All experiments were conducted at room temperature (20–24 °C).
source: All experiments were conducted at room temperature (20–24 °C).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Joint torques were measured with custom-built force sensors with strain gauges.
source: Joint torques were measured with custom-built force sensors with strain gauges.
evidence: This describes the measurement apparatus.

claim: The measured force [mN] was calibrated from the force-sensor value [V] with weights of known mass (0.2–5 g).
source: Prior to the experiments, the measured force [mN] was calibrated from the force-sensor value [V] with weights of known mass (0.2–5 g).
evidence: This describes the calibration procedure.

claim: Two small insect pins attached to the tip of the force transducer held the middle part of the femur of the middle leg.
source: Two small insect pins attached to the tip of the force transducer held the middle part of the femur of the middle leg (Figure 1A right).
evidence: This describes the experimental setup with reference to figure.

claim: The length between the ThC or CTr joints and the attachment point at the femur was measured and used as the moment arm for the calculation of torque.
source: The length between the ThC or CTr joints and the attachment point at the femur was measured and used as the moment arm for the calculation of torque.
evidence: This describes the torque calculation method.

claim: A custom-built electrical stimulator was developed for stimulating muscles.
source: We developed a custom-built electrical stimulator for stimulating muscles (Figure 1A left).
evidence: This describes the experimental apparatus.

claim: An extension circuit board was designed for Raspberry Pi 3 B+, including isolated 8-channel PWM signal outputs.
source: An extension circuit board was designed for Raspberry Pi 3 B+ (Raspberry Pi Foundation), including isolated 8-channel PWM signal outputs.
evidence: This describes the technical implementation.

claim: The parameters of the PWM signals, for example, frequency (1–120 Hz) and duty ratio (0 to 100%), were changed using a Raspberry Pi microprocessor.
source: The parameters of the PWM signals, for example, frequency (1–120 Hz) and duty ratio (0 to 100%), were changed using a Raspberry Pi microprocessor.
evidence: This describes the experimental control system.

claim: The amplitude of the output voltage (0–9 V) was changed using variable resistors on the circuit board.
source: The amplitude of the output voltage (0–9 V) was changed using variable resistors on the circuit board
evidence: This describes the voltage control mechanism.

claim: Burst duration is one of two key parameters for controlling isometric muscle-contraction force because the muscle essentially acts as a second-order low-pass filter.
source: Owing to the slow activation dynamics of an insect muscle, burst duration is one of two key parameters for controlling isometric muscle-contraction force because the muscle essentially acts as a second-order low-pass filter (Harischandra et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citation support regarding muscle properties.

claim: The pulse frequency is the other key parameter for controlling muscle contraction force.
source: The pulse frequency is the other key parameter, which can be held constant because burst duration alone is sufficient to effectively control joint torques in the range of 0–1.0 [s].
evidence: This is stated as a methodological choice.

claim: A pair of stimulation electrodes was implanted into each muscle through two small holes in the cuticle.
source: A pair of stimulation electrodes was implanted into each muscle through two small holes in the cuticle.
evidence: This describes the electrode implantation procedure.

claim: Holes were pierced using an insect pin, and wires were fixed with dental glue.
source: Holes were pierced using an insect pin, and wires were fixed with dental glue (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the surgical procedure.

claim: The stimulation electrodes were thin silver wires (A-M Systems, diameter = 127 µm, without insulation; 178 µm with Teflon insulation).
source: The stimulation electrodes were thin silver wires (A-M Systems, diameter = 127 µm, without insulation; 178 µm with Teflon insulation).
evidence: This describes the electrode specifications.

claim: The correctness of the electrode implantation was verified through triggered resistance reflexes.
source: The correctness of the electrode implantation was verified through triggered resistance reflexes, which are responses to imposed movements of the ThC and CTr joints for the corresponding muscles.
evidence: This describes the verification procedure.

claim: The parameter set with a frequency of 50 Hz and a duty ratio of 30% would allow continuous and effective torque generation.
source: We determined the parameter set with a frequency of 50 Hz and a duty ratio of 30%, which would allow continuous and effective torque generation in a pre-experiment.
evidence: This describes the parameter selection based on preliminary experiments.

claim: Applying voltages ranging between 1 and 4 V did not induce fatigue.
source: Furthermore, we confirmed that applying voltages ranging between 1 and 4 V did not induce fatigue.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental observations.

claim: Even after a large number of electrical stimulations of the muscles, no significant biological damage to the stick insect nor any fatigue or warm-up effects were observed.
source: Notably, even after such a large number of electrical stimulations of the muscles, we did not observe any significant biological damage to the stick insect nor any fatigue or warm-up effects.
evidence: This is stated based on experimental observations.

claim: The WAIC is a measure of the degree to which an estimate of the predictive distribution is accurate relative to the true distribution.
source: The WAIC is a measure of the degree to which an estimate of the predictive distribution is accurate relative to the true distribution (Watanabe, 2018).
evidence: This defines the WAIC metric with citation.

claim: The smaller (or more negative) the WAIC index, the higher the predictive value of the model variant.
source: The smaller (or more negative) the WAIC index, the higher the predictive value of the model variant.
evidence: This explains the interpretation of WAIC values.

claim: The model with the smallest WAIC value was considered the most appropriate predictive model in terms of predictivity for a new animal.
source: From the models described above, the model with the smallest WAIC value was considered the most appropriate predictive model in terms of predictivity for a new animal.
evidence: This describes the model selection criterion.
